key_insight: Framing surface meshes as probability measures and optimizing their Wasserstein gradient flow with an Adam-style optimizer (AdamFlow) yields fast, robust surface registration that balances speed and noise resilience.
problem_solved: Bridges the trade-off between computational efficiency (local point matching) and robustness/global alignment (optimal-transport approaches) in medical surface registration.
method: Represent surface meshes as probability measures / weighted point clouds and define alignment via a Wasserstein (optimal transport) energy.
Derive a discretized Wasserstein gradient flow to evolve source surfaces toward targets while preserving global structure and robustness to noise.
Introduce an Adam-based solver (AdamFlow) to accelerate convergence, stabilize noisy gradients, and reduce runtime compared with standard gradient-flow solvers.
impact: Provides a practical registration method that is both fast and robust for anatomical shape analysis, enabling scalable preprocessing and improved downstream ML applications in medical imaging.
visual_elements: Before/after overlay of two anatomical surfaces (source vs registered target) to show alignment quality.
Schematic of Wasserstein mass transport between surfaces with arrows illustrating the gradient flow evolution.
Convergence/runtime comparison chart (AdamFlow vs baseline methods) plotting registration error vs time or iterations.
Pipeline diagram: mesh → probability measure → Wasserstein gradient flow → AdamFlow optimizer → registered mesh.
paper_title: AdamFlow: Adam-based Wasserstein Gradient Flows for Surface Registration in Medical Imaging
paper_authors: Qiang Ma, Qingjie Meng, Xin Hu, Yicheng Wu, Wenjia Bai
